- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) or shows recent volatility, model often overshoots after spikes; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak observed in 3–5 prior days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from highs), model overreacts; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is > 10% above recent 7-day average, and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 5–10% to align with mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates > 5% from model in first 5 days, adjust remaining forecast downward linearly (e.g., slope = -0.05 per day) to reflect trend correction.
- If sentiment history includes 2+ consecutive negative values, model tends to underestimate; add 1–3% to forecast to compensate for sentiment-driven underreaction.
